Schedule an appointment: what happens, step by step

Our Schedule an appointment button opens Luay Sadqi’s page on PlanEnroll, a consumer site built by Integrity that connects to the system we use for client records. You create a profile, add your doctors, prescriptions and pharmacy, and ask for your meeting. This page explains each step and why we ask you to do it this way.

Reviewed by Luay Sadqi, Licensed Agent · NPN 21370662 · Updated November 2026

Schedule an appointment Call (301) 615-8289

What happens after you select Schedule an appointment

  1. PlanEnroll opens with Luay’s name at the top. You should see Luay Sadqi, Licensed Insurance Agent, NPN 21370662, Tysons, VA. That is how you know you are on our page.
  2. Choose Schedule an Appointment or Get Synced. PlanEnroll asks you to sign in. If you do not have a profile yet, choose Sign up and create one with your email address and a password.
  3. Enter your details. New clients are asked for their pharmacy, doctors, prescriptions and current coverage.
  4. Choose how to meet. PlanEnroll asks whether you prefer to meet over the phone, at our office in Tysons or at your home.
  5. Choose the type of meeting. Pick Life, Health or Annuities, and 30 or 60 minutes. The table below shows which one fits what you want to talk about. If you pick Health, you complete a short Scope of Appointment form at this step.
  6. Pick a day and time. You see our open times. The first one offered is at least 24 hours ahead. To talk sooner, call (301) 615-8289 or text (571) 354-0146.
  7. You get a confirmation. PlanEnroll confirms by email and text, with a link to add the meeting to your calendar and a link to cancel.
  8. We read it before we talk. Your profile syncs to our client records, so the conversation starts from your information.
Creating a profile does not enroll you in anything. It stores what you entered and lets you ask for a meeting. Choosing a plan is a separate step, and it is always your decision.

Which type of meeting to choose

ChooseIf you want to talk about
HealthMedicare Advantage, Medicare Supplement, Part D drug plans, dental, vision and hearing, hospital indemnity, cancer and critical illness, or health insurance under 65
LifeFinal expense, indexed universal life, term life, whole life or mortgage protection
AnnuitiesAnnuities, or rolling a 401(k), 403(b), TSP or IRA into one

Life insurance and annuities are a separate meeting from a Medicare meeting. If you want both, schedule each one.

Why we ask you to complete the forms first

Plans are compared against your own doctors and prescriptions

Two people in the same ZIP code can need different plans because they see different doctors and take different medications. When your list is already in your profile, we can check each plan against it instead of talking in general terms.

You enter it once, in your own words

Drug names, doses and doctors’ names are easy to mishear on a phone call. Typing them yourself keeps them accurate, and you do not have to repeat them.

Medicare rules require a record before we meet

Before a licensed agent meets with you about Medicare Advantage or Part D plans, federal rules require a record of the products you agreed to discuss. It is called a Scope of Appointment (see 42 CFR 422.2264). It does not enroll you in a plan and does not obligate you to enroll. PlanEnroll collects it in the same process, so it is done before your meeting.

You can update it whenever something changes

If a prescription or a doctor changes, sign in to your profile and submit the new information. We will see the update.

What to have next to you

  • Your prescriptions, with the dose and how often you take each one.
  • The names of the doctors and specialists you want to keep.
  • The pharmacy you use.
  • Your current insurance cards, so you can enter your current coverage.

You do not need to choose a plan before you schedule. That is what the meeting is for.

What our own website asks for

The forms on honorbrook-insurance.com ask for contact details only: your name, phone number, email address and ZIP code. Health details belong in your PlanEnroll profile. PlanEnroll is operated by Integrity, so its privacy policy and terms apply to what you enter there.

Common questions

Scheduling questions

Does creating a PlanEnroll profile enroll me in a plan?
No. A profile stores the details you enter and lets you ask for a meeting. Enrolling in a plan is a separate decision that you make later, after you have compared your options.
Is there a charge for scheduling or for your help?
No. Our help is free to you. Carriers pay us a commission when we place a policy, and your premium is the same whether you work with us or enroll on your own.
What is a Scope of Appointment?
It is a record of which products you agreed to talk about with a licensed agent. Medicare rules require it before an agent meets with you about Medicare Advantage or Part D plans. It does not enroll you in anything and does not obligate you to enroll.
Who receives what I enter?
Your profile is tied to Luay Sadqi’s PlanEnroll page, so it reaches Honorbrook. PlanEnroll is operated by Integrity, and its own privacy policy and terms apply to what you enter there.
Can I change my doctors or prescriptions later?
Yes. Sign in to your PlanEnroll profile and submit the updated information. It is worth doing whenever a prescription or doctor changes.
What if I already have a PlanEnroll profile?
Choose Sign In instead of creating a new profile, then continue from there.
